subject.title: fix(cli-runner): sweep orphaned bundle MCP temp dirs at gateway startup

question: Is PID plus Linux boot identity an acceptable ownership contract for supported multi-gateway and shared-temporary-directory deployments, with possible stale-directory over-retention, or must stronger process namespace/start-time identity land before this startup sweeper merges?
rationale: The patch is mechanically sound for the demonstrated host topology, but only maintainers can define which multi-process and container topologies the gateway lifecycle must safely support and whether fail-closed run rejection is the intended permanent contract.

options.title: Accept the bounded contract
options.body: Rebase, rerun the relevant gates, and merge with the documented safe-direction over-retention limitation.

options.title: Strengthen owner identity first
options.body: Add PID namespace or process-start identity and focused shared-temporary-root coverage before enabling startup deletion.

options.title: Pause the startup janitor
options.body: Keep callback cleanup only until a less process-inventory-dependent reclamation design is available.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded contract
recommendation.body: Rebase, rerun the relevant gates, and merge with the documented safe-direction over-retention limitation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent work connects this contributor to bundled-MCP disposal, process cleanup, and gateway lifecycle invariants.
